title: 7th AOYF Human Rights Photography Prize: Post-Truth, Reality in Question
organiser: Act On Your Future Foundation, with the Centre de la photographie Genève
eligibility: Artists of any nationality or residence
summary: A human rights photography prize on truth and doubt in a world of manipulated and AI-made images. Five finalists get production support and a summer 2027 show in Geneva, and the winner takes CHF 10,000.

evidence.deadline: Date limite de candidature : 20 décembre 2026 à 23h59

title: Devotion — Online Group Exhibition
summary: An online group show on devotion in its tender and darker forms, curated by Polaroid emulsion-lift artist Laura Barth. Analogue work only; the exhibition opens at the end of November.

title: Call for Photographs: Our Bodies that are Unruly
eligibility: Anyone aged 18 or over, based anywhere

rights.summary: Copyright stays with the photographer; Autograph may show selected images to promote the project on its website, social media and in press.

summary: Autograph wants pictures of the body as a place of resistance and self-definition, from new work to old family snaps. Its favourites go into an online gallery; up to three images each, and film scans are welcome.

evidence.deadline: The deadline to apply is 10am, Monday 7 December 2026
evidence.fee: The call for photographs is free to enter
evidence.rights: Copyright for any images you submit will remain with you.

title: FUTURES Nordic Talents 2027
organiser: Copenhagen Photo Festival, with the FUTURES platform
eligibility: Young emerging artists resident in a Nordic country for the past 12 months
summary: Copenhagen Photo Festival nominates four young Nordic photographers to the European FUTURES network for 2027, with a €500 artist fee, mentoring, exhibition calls and a screening at the festival.

evidence.deadline: 1 December 2026 · Deadline for the open call
evidence.fee: You pay a fee of DKK 100.

title: NeverAtHome Open Call for artists based in Austria
organiser: NeverAtHome, with the Austrian Cultural Forums
eligibility: Artists and creative practitioners based in Austria
summary: Artists based in Austria propose new work tied to one of 27 cities with an Austrian Cultural Forum, presented at that Forum during 2027 before a joint Vienna show the year after.

title: A Day in Your Life 2026
eligibility: Residents of Kensington and Chelsea or Westminster, aged five and over
summary: A community photography competition for two central London boroughs, tied to free workshops and mentoring; prizes include a short course at UAL.

title: Earth Photo 2027
organiser: Earth Photo (Parker Harris, Royal Geographical Society and Forestry England, with Photoworks)
eligibility: Anyone worldwide, for work made in the last five years
summary: An international award for still and moving images about the planet, from climate impacts to restoration. Prizes include cash awards, a residency and a Royal Geographical Society exhibition, plus awards for entrants aged 25 or under.

evidence.fee: Earth Photo is free to enter

title: FoMe Fotografía Mexicana 2027: Intuition
organiser: FoMe, Mexico City International Photography Fair
eligibility: Photographers anywhere, one proposal each

rights.summary: Artists keep their copyright; the 50 selected works are offered for sale at the fair, and the prize does not buy the work or its rights.

summary: A new photography fair in Mexico City picks 50 single images on the theme Intuition to print, mount and show for sale during Art Week in February 2027, with a MXN 120,000 prize for one of them.

evidence.rights: El premio no implica la adquisición de la obra ni la cesión de derechos de autor

title: Form Photo Award x UNSEEN 2027
summary: An open-theme award for contemporary photography whose winners show at UNSEEN during Art Rotterdam in March 2027. Longlisted entrants are published in Form Magazine.

title: Let Our Hearts Speak
summary: A call for a collective publication on Eastern Europe as memory, migration and inheritance as much as geography, shaped by bell hooks’ writing on love.

title: GRAIN Projects National Open Call: Young Photographers
eligibility: Photographers aged 18 to 26 living in England
summary: A £2,000 commission, plus £500 towards a public showing, for a young photographer to make new work about their own life, friends and the pressures they face, developed with GRAIN in Birmingham.

title: 2027 Anja Niedringhaus Courage in Photojournalism Award
eligibility: Women, nonbinary and gender nonconforming photojournalists, freelance or staff
summary: An award honouring women, nonbinary and gender nonconforming photojournalists who work in dangerous conditions. Candidates can self-nominate or be put forward with a portfolio of recent and career work.

title: Kraszna-Krausz Book Awards 2027
eligibility: Photobooks with substantial text published in 2026, self-published titles included (print run of 100 or more)
summary: Annual awards for the best new books on photography and the moving image. A photobook with real text published during 2026 can be entered by its publisher, its author or a self-publisher.

title: Mesnographies 2027: The pursuit of happiness
summary: A free open-air photography festival in Les Mesnuls, France, calling for work on what happiness means. Its site gives no date for the call.

title: Walk of Water Photostory Contest: Out of Sight
summary: A photostory contest run with UN water and environment programmes on water and health, with its main prize aimed at the rarely photographed world of wastewater and sanitation.

title: Chennai Photo Biennale International Open Call, Edition 3

fee.note: per single image outside South Asia; €15 per photo story

eligibility: Anyone, from anywhere, on any subject

rights.summary: Copyright stays with the photographer; every entry may be kept at low resolution in the biennale’s research archive without payment, and selected work used to promote the open call.

summary: The biennale’s international call for single images and series on any subject, run with SIGMA India.

evidence.fee: Rest of the World - Single Image: 8EUR Per entry
evidence.rights: For all submissions, copyright holders will grant the organizers non-exclusive use of low-resolution pictures in a public archive for its research and educational activities, without any remuneration being due.

title: Phodar International Photo Festival Biennale, 14th edition: Traces Remain
eligibility: Professional and amateur photographers over 18, from any country

rights.summary: Copyright stays with the photographer; entries may be shown and sub-licensed to the press only in connection with the award and its exhibitions.

summary: A biennial competition in Sofia for a series of 8 to 20 photographs on the theme Traces Remain, with a grand prize, a debut prize for newcomers and an award for humanistic photography.

evidence.rights: Copyright of the images will remain at all times with the photographer.

title: Winston Taylor Irish Photo Prize 2027
organiser: Photo Museum Ireland, with Winston Taylor
eligibility: Photographers from across the island of Ireland, Northern Ireland included
summary: Ireland’s largest photography prize, on the theme Change, with €30,000 across a main prize, runner-up awards and a bursary, and a spring 2027 exhibition at Photo Museum Ireland in Dublin.

title: Photoville Festival 2027: exhibition proposals
eligibility: Photo-based artists, collectives and organisations anywhere
summary: New York’s free outdoor photography festival invites exhibition proposals in any genre for three weeks in Brooklyn Bridge Park and other city spaces from May 2027, with production paid for selected independent artists.

title: Photoworks New Year Commission 2027
eligibility: Photographers and lens-based artists anywhere
summary: A £500 commission for one playful image to welcome 2027, shared by Photoworks online, sent to its industry mailing list and printed as a postcard in every shop order next year.

title: P5 Photo Poetry Pamphlet Series, volumes 5 and 6
eligibility: Artists at any stage, anywhere, working with photography and poetry alone or together
summary: Photoworks will publish two more photo and poetry pamphlets in spring 2027, each paying the artist £1,000 plus copies, for existing unpublished work that pairs images with text.

evidence.deadline: Apply by midnight (GMT) on Wednesday 27 January 2027

title: THE DRAFT — Tessa Boffin: Where We Touch the Archive
organiser: Devonshire Collective, Photoworks, BACKLIT and Aspex Portsmouth
eligibility: LGBTQIA+ artists, writers, researchers and activists

rights.summary: Copyright stays with the contributor; the organisers get a non-exclusive licence to reproduce contributions in the publication and related project materials.

summary: A queer publication that grows over a UK touring exhibition about artist Tessa Boffin. Contributors share something that already exists, such as a photograph or contact sheet, along with a question for the next person.

evidence.rights: You retain copyright of your contribution.

title: Pride Photo 2027
eligibility: Photographers of any age or level, worldwide
summary: An annual contest for photography about LGBTQIA+ lives, taking single images or a series of three to fifteen. Each selected work earns €500 and is shown in an international exhibition from spring 2027; fully AI-generated images are not accepted.

title: Dutch Talent Project Grant
eligibility: Emerging photographers based, studying or educated in the Netherlands
summary: Five emerging photographers each get €3,000 to make new work on the theme Vibrance, then show it as a work in progress at Rotterdam Photo 2027 with curatorial guidance.

title: RPS International Photography Exhibition 168

fee.note: per entry after one free single image; £27 RPS members, £20 under-30s

eligibility: Anyone, of any age or level of practice
summary: The Royal Photographic Society's long-running annual open exhibition. Selected work tours UK venues and is up for cash awards, including one for under-30s; shortlisted entrants send prints for the final round.

evidence.deadline: Entry will close for new entries at 23:59 GMT on Tuesday 15 December 2026
evidence.fee: Subsequent entries are subject to payment: Standard £35, RPS Member £27, Under 30 years old £20.

title: The City Series: London

fee.note: minimum, pay what you can; some free places

rights.summary: Copyright stays with the photographer, but Shutter Hub may reproduce and publish any entry without payment for the book and its promotion.

summary: Pictures of London for the next book in Shutter Hub’s city photobook series, launching in early 2027 with an event for everyone who entered. Up to ten images each.

evidence.fee: Pay what you can, minimum fee of £15.
evidence.rights: Shutter Hub reserves the right to display, reproduce and publish in any media any entry, without payment, for the purpose of the publication and its promotion and publicity.

title: FOTODOKS Open Call 2027
summary: Munich’s documentary photography festival wants projects on care and its politics for its October 2027 edition. Selected photographers are paid an artist fee plus travel costs.

title: Textile Exchange Photography Competition 2026
summary: A competition for photographs and short films about regeneration across the fashion and textile industry, from farming to finished garments. Its own page turned us away, so dates and fees are unconfirmed.

title: Human Impact Awards 2026
summary: Wex’s annual award for photographs about people and their effect on the world, with an open brief that runs from community and identity to everyday connection.
